segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. What CLI tools and containerized services actually need day-to-day (argument parsing, stdin, environment config, exit codes). Prioritized because the long-term project direction favors CLI/microservice use cases. `console.log`/`.error` already write to stdout/stderr respectively — see [CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md) — the gaps below are everything *else* a CLI program needs.

caveats: Mirrors C's `argv` directly (`argv[0]` is the binary's own path), not Node's two-prefix convention — see [ADR-00002](../adr/ADR-00002.md)
An out-of-range `process.argv[i]` read yields `""` (falsy), not Node's `undefined` and not the general array bounds throw ([ADR-00425](../adr/ADR-00425.md))

notes: Both dot and bracket notation; returns a possibly-null string (same convention as `.find()`), so `process.env.X ?? "default"` works
caveats: A missing variable reads as `null`, not `undefined` — `process.env.MISSING === null` is `true` (Node: `false`), `console.log` prints `null`, and `typeof process.env.MISSING` is `'string'` (Node: `'undefined'`); `?? default`, `=== undefined` and comparisons against a string all behave as in Node (a missing value equals only `undefined`/`null`, never a string, and orders as `false` — [ADR-00724](../adr/ADR-00724.md)), but `typeof` guards diverge.

notes: Calls C `exit()`; never returns, code after it is correctly unreachable

`process.readLineSync()` — one line via POSIX `getline()` (handles arbitrarily long lines), stripped of its trailing `\n`/`\r\n`. Returns `null` at EOF (same possibly-null convention as `process.env`). See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).
See [FILE-SYSTEM.md](FILE-SYSTEM.md)

caveats: Options support only `{ cwd, encoding: 'utf8' }` ([ADR-00589](../adr/ADR-00589.md)) — `cwd` chdir's the child before exec; `env`/`timeout`/`stdio` overrides are still deferred
stderr is inherited (visible on the terminal live), not captured
notes: Node's `child_process.execFileSync`, not `execSync`: `fork()`+`execvp()`s `file` directly with no shell involved, so shell metacharacters in `args` are never interpreted
Returns captured stdout as a string; throws a catchable `Error` on a non-zero exit status or a signal death. See [ADR-00025](../adr/ADR-00025.md).
Current working directory, via POSIX `getcwd(NULL, 0)` (auto-sizing). See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md).

Changes the current working directory via POSIX `chdir()`. Throws a catchable `Error` (same "`<opDesc>` '`<path>`': `<strerror>`" shape `fs.*`'s failures already use) if the path doesn't exist or isn't a directory. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md).
The current process ID, via POSIX `getpid()`. A property read, not a call, matching `process.argv`. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md).

A pure compile-time constant (`"darwin"`/`"linux"`/`"win32"`/...) baked in from the Go compiler's own `runtime.GOOS` — no runtime code at all, since this compiler doesn't cross-compile. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md).
A compile-time constant (`"arm64"`/`"x64"`/...) from the Go compiler's `runtime.GOARCH`, exactly like `process.platform` ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md))

The absolute, symlink-resolved path of the running executable — the compiled program is itself the binary (no separate runtime), resolved via `_NSGetExecutablePath`+`realpath` (macOS) / `/proc/self/exe` (Linux), so it's always absolute like Node's, not a raw `argv[0]` ([ADR-00395](../adr/ADR-00395.md))

caveats: The one-shot `--trace-warnings` hint line Node prints is deliberately omitted, and the `'warning'`-event `Error` carries only `name`/`message` (not `code`/`detail`) — the fixed error-object shape ([ADR-00580](../adr/ADR-00580.md))
notes: Writes `(node:<pid>) [<code>] <type>: <message>` to stderr (the `[code]` only when a `code` is given), `type` defaulting to `"Warning"`, then a `<detail>` line when a `detail` is given; the options-object form is `{ type?, code?, detail? }` ([ADR-00580](../adr/ADR-00580.md))
Like Node's always-on default printer, additionally invokes any `process.on('warning', …)` listener with the warning as an `Error` ([ADR-00395](../adr/ADR-00395.md)/[ADR-00401](../adr/ADR-00401.md))

Sends `signal` (defaults to `15`/`SIGTERM`, matching real Node) to `pid` via POSIX `kill()`. Throws a catchable `Error` if the target process doesn't exist or the signal can't be sent; signal `0` is the standard POSIX "does this process exist" check and never actually delivers a signal. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md).

The signal may be a name (`'SIGTERM'`, `'SIGINT'`, …) as in Node — a literal resolves at compile time against the host's `os.constants.signals` table, a dynamic string at run time; an unknown literal name is a compile error, the counterpart of Node's `ERR_UNKNOWN_SIGNAL` ([ADR-00729](../adr/ADR-00729.md))

On Windows every signal except `0` terminates the target unconditionally (libuv's `TerminateProcess`), exit code 1 — a `SIGTERM` listener in the target never runs, as in Node ([ADR-00728](../adr/ADR-00728.md))
caveats: The thrown message carries the signal number (`kill(pid=…, signal=15)`), not the name Node prints
Text-only (byte-string, not binary-safe past an embedded null — same scope narrowing `console.log`'s own string formatting already has)

Beyond `.write`, `.isTTY` (a real `isatty(fd)` probe on all three stdio handles — [ADR-00424](../adr/ADR-00424.md)), and `.columns`/`.rows` (a live `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` read — [ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)), `process.stdout`/`stderr` expose no other stream surface (no `'drain'`)
notes: Unlike `console.log`/`.error` (always a trailing newline), a plain write of exactly `s` with nothing appended — useful for a progress indicator or assembling one line from several pieces

`stdout` goes through buffered `printf` (matching `console.log`'s own fd=1 convention, so output ordering against `console.log` calls elsewhere in the same program stays correct); `stderr` goes through unbuffered `dprintf` (matching `console.error`'s own fd=2 convention)

caveats: Off a non-TTY (piped/redirected) returns an 80x24 fallback rather than Node's `undefined` — this compiler has no clean undefined-number ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md))
notes: A live `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` read on each access (never cached, matching Node); pair with `process.on('SIGWINCH')` to repaint on resize
Available on both `process.stdout` and `process.stderr`

caveats: A no-op when fd 0 is not a terminal (`tcgetattr` fails; on Windows, `GetConsoleMode` fails) — guard on `process.stdin.isTTY` first, as every TUI does
notes: Raw mode disables signal generation (`ISIG`), so Ctrl-C stops delivering `SIGINT` and arrives as the raw byte `3` for the program to handle — matching Node/libuv `UV_TTY_MODE_RAW` exactly
Auto-restore on a crash/uncaught exception is the application's responsibility (same footgun as Node); `setRawMode(false)` restores the state captured on the first enable

Routes through an embedded C shim compiled against the platform's own `<termios.h>`, so the glibc/Darwin `struct termios` layout difference is sidestepped by construction ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)); on Windows the same shim uses the console-mode API (line input/echo/processed input off, VT input on, so arrow keys arrive as ESC `[` A there too) — verified in the suite under a ConPTY pseudo-console ([ADR-00727](../adr/ADR-00727.md))
Pair with `process.stdin.on('data')` (event-driven, the Node-idiomatic raw loop) or with `klain:tty` `readByte`/`readKey` (synchronous)

caveats: Bespoke, non-Node surface under the explicit `klain:` specifier — Node has no synchronous single-key read (it uses `process.stdin.on('data')` events)
Blocking reads on fd 0; do not mix with `process.stdin.on('data')` in the same run, which puts fd 0 in non-blocking mode (a synchronous read would then see EOF-on-EAGAIN)
notes: `readByte()` returns one byte (or -1 at EOF); `readKey()` returns one `read()`'s whole burst as a string, so an escape sequence like an arrow key (ESC `[` A) is a single key ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md))
`readKey(timeoutMs)` polls: it waits at most `timeoutMs` and returns `""` if no key arrived — the tick a self-refreshing `klain:tui` loop redraws on ([ADR-00520](../adr/ADR-00520.md))

caveats: Compound assignment (`process.env.X += …`) is a clean rejection
notes: `setenv(key, String(val), overwrite)` ([ADR-00333](../adr/ADR-00333.md)); a written variable is inherited by child processes
`delete process.env.KEY` unsets the variable for real ([ADR-00487](../adr/ADR-00487.md))

caveats: The handler runs from ordinary control flow at the top of the event loop's own iteration, never from real async signal context (on Windows the console control callback queues the signal and the loop's next wait, at most 50 ms away, delivers it on the main thread — [ADR-00728](../adr/ADR-00728.md))

Event name must be a compile-time string literal, exactly `'SIGINT'`/`'SIGTERM'`/`'SIGWINCH'`/`'SIGBREAK'` (dynamic event names are a clean compile error, matching `Object.hasOwn`'s dynamic-key rejection)

Windows, as in Node: `'SIGINT'` fires on Ctrl+C, `'SIGBREAK'` on Ctrl+Break, `'SIGTERM'` is accepted but never fires (`process.kill` terminates unconditionally); `'SIGBREAK'` is accepted on POSIX hosts and never raised there
Handler must be a zero-argument `() => void` closure, same shape `setTimeout`'s own callback requires
One handler slot per signal — registering the same signal twice overwrites the previous handler
Only fires while a `http.listen`-driven or timer-driven event loop is actively iterating; a plain synchronous script with neither has no loop to check from
notes: Lets a running program (e.g. an `http.listen` server) intercept a signal and shut down gracefully instead of dying immediately. See [TDD-00019](../tdd/TDD-00019.md)/[ADR-00079](../adr/ADR-00079.md), [HTTP-SERVER.md](HTTP-SERVER.md).

`'SIGWINCH'` (terminal resize) lets a TUI re-read `process.stdout.columns`/`.rows` and repaint on a window resize ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)); on Windows (no `SIGWINCH` signal) a read-only console-size watcher thread delivers it through the same loop path as the other signals, ~200 ms poll latency ([ADR-00749](../adr/ADR-00749.md))

caveats: `'uncaughtException'` runs the listener (suppressing the default `Uncaught:` print) but the process still exits (code 1) — the setjmp/longjmp exception model has already unwound to the top-level catch-all, so it can't resume execution like Node does
`'warning'` fires (with the warning as an `Error`) when `process.emitWarning` is called; the stderr print still happens too
No `'unhandledRejection'` yet (needs rejected-promise tracking)
One listener slot per event, arrow-literal only
notes: `'exit'` fires at normal end and from `process.exit()`, receiving the exit code; `process.exitCode = N` sets the deferred code a bare program returns; `process.exit()` with no argument uses it ([ADR-00334](../adr/ADR-00334.md)/[ADR-00401](../adr/ADR-00401.md))
`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` via the same layer as `performance.now()` ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md)); `hrtime()` → a `[seconds, nanoseconds]` tuple, `.bigint()` → total-nanoseconds bigint
`hrtime(prev)` returns the elapsed diff from a prior `[seconds, nanoseconds]` reading, applying Node's borrow when the nanosecond field would go negative ([ADR-00582](../adr/ADR-00582.md))

Direct POSIX credential reads returning a `number`, matching Node-on-POSIX ([ADR-00428](../adr/ADR-00428.md)); on Windows they are rejected at compile time, exactly as Node leaves them undefined there ([TDD-00177](../tdd/TDD-00177.md))

`rss` is the process's **instantaneous** resident set size in bytes — Darwin via `task_info(MACH_TASK_BASIC_INFO)`, Linux via `/proc/self/statm` — matching real Node's `rss` (which is also the live value, not a peak) ([ADR-00570](../adr/ADR-00570.md)/[ADR-00507](../adr/ADR-00507.md))
caveats: Only `rss` carries a real value; `heapTotal`/`heapUsed`/`external`/`arrayBuffers` report 0 — there is no managed V8 heap to measure in a native build, so they are returned zeroed rather than fabricated
Shares the one microtask FIFO with Promise reactions rather than draining strictly before them (Node keeps a separate nextTick queue ahead of promises); zero-argument `() => void` callback only
notes: Enqueued on the existing microtask queue ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md))

caveats: `versions` reports only honest values — `node`/`v8` (the pinned Node compatibility baseline, v22.11.0) and `klain` (this compiler's version); it deliberately omits bundled-lib keys this compiler doesn't ship (`uv`/`undici`/`icu`/…) rather than fabricate them
The real linked-library versions we *can* report truthfully (`openssl` under the OpenSSL backend, `zlib` when linked) are a follow-on — they need a runtime lib query + backend-aware linking
`node`/`v8` track the compatibility *ceiling* (the pinned test-corpus release); a `--node-compat` floor is deferred ([TDD-00136](../tdd/TDD-00136.md))
notes: `process.version` = `"v22.11.0"`; `process.versions` is a real object (`JSON.stringify`/field access/`Object.keys` all work), matching Node v22.11.0's `node`/`v8` verbatim ([ADR-00396](../adr/ADR-00396.md))

`versions.klain` is the compiler's own version, stamped at link time from the release tag by the release pipeline (`klainmain --version` prints the same value; a `make build` stamps `git describe`, a bare `go build` reports `0.0.0-dev`) — [ADR-00732](../adr/ADR-00732.md)
Seconds (a `double`) since process start, captured once at `main` entry via `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md))

caveats: `'data'` delivers each read chunk as a UTF-8 string, not a `Buffer` — no `setEncoding`, no binary mode
Flowing mode only (attaching `'data'` starts it) — no `.pause()`/`.resume()`/`.read()`/`'readable'`
One listener per event, arrow/function-expression literal only; callbacks fire synchronously from the dispatch, not via a microtask
notes: `process.stdin.on('data'/'end')` over a non-blocking fd 0 folded into the same `select()` loop as `readline`/`child_process` ([ADR-00339](../adr/ADR-00339.md)); `'data'` per read chunk, `'end'` once on EOF. Distinct from the blocking `process.readLineSync()` and the line-oriented `readline` module above

caveats: The listener callbacks fire synchronously from the event loop's dispatch, not deferred through a microtask queue (same as `child_process`)
One listener per event, an arrow/function-expression literal only; no line history/editing, no `SIGINT`/`'pause'`/`'resume'`, no completer
The `createInterface` options object is accepted but ignored — input is always stdin, output always stdout; one active interface at a time
notes: Non-blocking stdin (fd 0) folded into the same `select()` loop as `child_process` ([ADR-00323](../adr/ADR-00323.md)); emits one `'line'` per newline (CR stripped), flushes an unterminated final line on EOF then fires `'close'`. Distinct from the blocking `process.readLineSync()` above

caveats: The listener callbacks fire synchronously from the event loop's dispatch, not deferred through the microtask queue (`process.nextTick` — see the row above)
One listener per event, an arrow/function-expression literal only (the same posture as `Worker`); no `removeListener`

spawn's options support `{ cwd, shell, stdio: 'pipe' }` ([ADR-00433](../adr/ADR-00433.md), [ADR-00740](../adr/ADR-00740.md)) — `cwd` is real (child chdir); `shell: true` routes the command through the platform shell (`/bin/sh -c` / `cmd.exe /d /s /c`, honouring `%ComSpec%`) as one string (a shell *path*, a dynamic value, or `shell:true` with an args array are clean rejections); `env` fully replaces the child's environment (an object literal of string values, Node's non-merging semantics — [ADR-00762](../adr/ADR-00762.md)); `windowsHide` (literal bool) suppresses the child's console window on Windows (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) and is a no-op on POSIX ([ADR-00763](../adr/ADR-00763.md)); `timeout` (ms) kills the child via the event loop with `killSignal` (a literal name/number, default SIGTERM), surfacing as the `(null, '<signal>')` exit event ([ADR-00764](../adr/ADR-00764.md)); `detached` (literal bool) makes the child a new session/group leader — `setsid` on POSIX, `DETACHED_PROCESS` on Windows ([ADR-00765](../adr/ADR-00765.md)); `stdio` takes `'pipe'`/`'inherit'`/`'ignore'` as a string or a 3-element `[stdin, stdout, stderr]` array — inherit wires the fd to the parent's, ignore sends it to `/dev/null`/NUL ([ADR-00766](../adr/ADR-00766.md); fd numbers, `'ipc'` and streams are clean rejections); exec/execFile still take no options

`exec`/`execSync` pass the command line to the shell **verbatim** — embedded quotes survive (`exec('echo "hi"')`), matching Node; on Windows a `.bat`/`.cmd` spawned *without* a shell is refused, surfacing as the spawn `'error'` event (`EINVAL`) rather than run through an implicit `cmd.exe`, closing the CVE-2024-27980 argument-injection path ([ADR-00740](../adr/ADR-00740.md)/[ADR-00754](../adr/ADR-00754.md))
The `'error'` Error carries a `.message` (`spawn <reason>`) but not the Node `.code`/`.errno`/`.syscall`/`.path`/`.spawnargs` properties

A legacy `'exit'`/`'close'` listener that declares one non-nullable `number` param sees `0` (not `null`) on a signal death — a plain `number` can't hold `null`; type the param `number | null` for the faithful `null` ([ADR-00761](../adr/ADR-00761.md))
`child.kill` takes a signal *name* string only as a **literal** (resolved to the host's signal number at compile time) or a number; a dynamic signal-name string is a clean rejection
Handles and their buffered output are never freed (`-mm=manual`)
notes: fork()+execvp() with three pipes; the two read ends are non-blocking and fold into the same `select()` event loop as Worker/channel pipes ([ADR-00322](../adr/ADR-00322.md))

`spawn` streams (`child.stdout`/`stderr` `'data'`/`'end'`, `child.on('close'/'exit'/'error')`, `child.stdin.write`/`.end`, `child.pid`, `child.kill`, `child.unref()`/`ref()` — the loop-keepalive opt-out, [ADR-00767](../adr/ADR-00767.md)); `exec` runs via `/bin/sh -c` and `execFile` execvp's directly, both buffering into a single `(err, stdout, stderr)` callback

A spawn that fails to start (a missing command → `ENOENT`) emits the `'error'` event with an `Error` and **not** `'exit'` — detected via a close-on-exec status pipe on POSIX and `CreateProcessW`'s failure on Windows ([ADR-00754](../adr/ADR-00754.md))

The `'exit'`/`'close'` exit `code` is the child's real width: on Windows the full 32-bit value (`cmd /c exit 300` → `300`, an access violation → `3221225477`), on POSIX the 8-bit wait-status field (`300 & 0xff = 44`, as Node also reports there) ([ADR-00759](../adr/ADR-00759.md))

`'exit'`/`'close'` fire as `(code, signal)` like Node: a signal death gives `code = null` and the signal **name** (`'SIGTERM'`), a normal exit the integer code and `signal = null`. POSIX recovers the signal from the wait status (`WIFSIGNALED`/`WTERMSIG`); Windows from the signal `child.kill` recorded, since `TerminateProcess` leaves no signalled bit ([ADR-00761](../adr/ADR-00761.md), [TDD-00184](../tdd/TDD-00184.md))

caveats: Self-fork only: the path must be `__filename` or `process.argv[1]` (forking a *different* module would need a second compiled program — clean rejection); the options object must be an empty `{}`
Messages are strings (`send(obj)` is a clean rejection); one `'message'` listener per side
Bare `process.send` reads as a *boolean* forked-ness probe, not Node's function-or-undefined — `assert.strictEqual(process.send, undefined)`-style tests type-mismatch cleanly
`process.argv[i]` out-of-range reads yield `""` (falsy) rather than Node's `undefined` — the `argv[2] === 'child'` / `if (!argv[2])` idioms behave; a strict compare against `undefined` doesn't
notes: Node's own mechanism ([TDD-00141](../tdd/TDD-00141.md)/[ADR-00425](../adr/ADR-00425.md)): socketpair + re-exec of the current binary with `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` set; child argv layout `[exe, modulePath, ...args]` so extra args land at `argv[2]`; NDJSON string frames (embedded C, linked only when used)

Parent: `child.send(str)→bool`, `child.on('message'/'exit'/'close')`, `child.disconnect()`, inherited stdio; child: `process.send(str)→bool` (false unforked), `process.on('message')` (holds the event loop open while connected), `process.disconnect()`; `mustCall`-wrapped listeners contextually typed

caveats: Options object supports `{ cwd, encoding: 'utf8' }` only (no `env`/`timeout`/`input`/`shell`/`stdio` — clean rejections); results are strings (the `encoding: 'utf8'` shape), not Buffers
`spawnSync`'s result carries `status`/`stdout`/`stderr`/`pid` only — no `signal`/`error`/`output` fields (a signal death folds into `status` as `128+signal`)

`execSync`/`execFileSync` throw `Command failed: <command>` on a non-zero exit status ([ADR-00753](../adr/ADR-00753.md)), but the thrown plain `Error` does not yet carry the `.status`/`.stdout`/`.stderr` ExecException properties — use `spawnSync().status` when the exit code or captured output of a failing command is needed
notes: One embedded C core ([ADR-00411](../adr/ADR-00411.md)): fork + execvp with both stdio pipes poll-multiplexed to completion (no deadlock when a child fills stderr while stdout drains), then a blocking waitpid; `execSync` runs via `/bin/sh -c`
`execSync`/`execFileSync` throw on a non-zero exit and return the captured stdout only on success, matching Node ([ADR-00753](../adr/ADR-00753.md))
Distinct from the bespoke `process.execFileSync` above (which throws on failure and inherits stderr)
